A Codex PreCompact hook saying `Managed carry-respawn is QUEUED` proves admission only. Read the owner's `psu-pty/<owner>.events.jsonl` for the subsequent `respawn-failed` outcome before attributing repeated interruptions to the Codex model or account.

On 2026-10-24, WI-6554700010027627 reproduced the same actual owner/ADV home-repair request returning HTTP 500 through 9071 and HTTP 200 through 3170. The failing body named three su.md observation headings absent from the serving renderer's SU_TILES. These were prompt/source build skew. `ensureCodexHomeViaOperator` preserved the HTTP failure classification; `recycleChild` refused replacement before stopping the original child. The hook's queued acknowledgement then remained the visible outcome.

The durable source repair in `adv/sessions.ts` recognizes only the typed `su-tiling-unsound` error and uses the verified prior launch artifact. `pinnedSuRecoveryPrompt` checks replay integrity and receipt revision; ordinary SU sessions can opt into this recovery without a selected identity. Existing selected-source recovery keeps its original defaults. Missing artifacts, tampered receipts, unrelated errors, and identity-admission failures remain refusals. Recovery returns `pinned-renderer-skew` and does not claim a new identity activation. The PTY also reports failed home preparation after admission, including its HTTP status. Historical source publication: core repair f76335e2c3; terminal diagnostic a9e3ac8e30.

Verification: the endpoint regression failed before the change (two failures); the endpoint and artifact suites passed 72 tests afterward. Runtime MJS verification used Node syntax, declaration generation and the PTY regression; it is not a whole-repository TypeScript claim. ## Supported recovery while an old writer is incompatible

This is a temporary operational recovery. Permanent completion still requires publishing a compatible serving writer and verifying affected older sessions there. Use the canonical lifecycle tools; never raw signals, PTY control-file edits, a fork, or a second live writer.

1. Read the target's latest work-item checkpoints and actual launch metadata. Save its exact logical owner, native/ADV identity, model and effort, account routing, visible/headless placement, modes, mission and claims. Ask an active target to checkpoint and reply READY. If it cannot answer because it is stuck, establish a safe boundary from saved state, edit-lock ownership and concrete running-job evidence; retain unfinished or failed verification faithfully.
2. Call audited `fleet:kill { owner, reason }` and require a successful retirement receipt. A live or non-wakeable presence reading alone is not permission to launch a competing writer. The successor route refuses a still-live predecessor; honor that refusal.
3. Use `capability:launch-agent { successor:{agentId:<same-owner>}, mcpTarget:'spawn-host', ...savedProfile, idempotencyKey }` against the verified compatible runtime. In this incident that runtime was local 3170; this port is historical evidence, not a universal routing constant. Pin the CLI route with `--url` when needed. Preserve the original model/effort, account and placement explicitly, especially for solo agents: omitted successor settings need not inherit the resume profile. Restore AUTO only where it was already authorized.
4. Verify a real native model/tool turn and a concrete read of the target's saved checkpoint. Process-open evidence alone is insufficient. Read host metadata and the per-session config for settings that presence does not expose. Keep `firstTurn:null` unknown until actual pickup evidence arrives.
5. Retirement can release claims and deactivate a loop. The same owner reclaims only its released, unheld original work and resumes its original authorized mission; it must honor any new live holder. Restore only previously authorized ongoing work. Do not acquire LIVE_GATE_OPS merely because an older session once held it.

Two headless pilots and a visible pilot produced real pickup receipts before applying this recovery to owner2185's explicit targets. su-f9dd6 resumed as native01a16f09-ad75-74e0-814f-2e801f04551a (ADV51591); su-a7fa0 resumed as native01a16f0f-7a3c-7a82-ba11-8640c9d47cfa (ADV51595). Both retained their logical owner, AUTO/self mission, gpt-6.1-sol with xhigh effort, auto account routing and visible placement. Exact receipts and checkpoint references are on WI-6554700010027627.

At 17:55:53Z on 2026-10-24, the original affected owner9597/ADV51499 still returned HTTP 500 through normal 9071 with the same three SU_TILES headings. A contemporaneous home repair for this investigator's newer self session ADV51523 succeeded through the same route. That newer-session success does not establish older-session repair.
